title: Mosquito-Borne Diseases on the Rise
author: News Desk
excerpt: Mosquito-borne diseases like dengue, chikungunya, and Zika are spreading faster worldwide due to climate change, urbanization, and invasive species.
content:
Global Spread

Mosquito-borne diseases like dengue, chikungunya, and Zika are becoming more prevalent worldwide. Factors such as climate change, urbanization, and increased international travel are contributing to their spread. (source)

Europe

In 2025, Europe recorded a significant increase in mosquito-borne diseases. The ECDC reported 27 chikungunya outbreaks, marking a new record. The spread of the Asian tiger mosquito (Aedes albopictus) has led to rising cases of dengue and chikungunya in countries like France, Spain, and Greece. (source)

United States

In the U.S., invasive mosquito species such as Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus have been reported in several states, including California and Massachusetts. These mosquitoes can transmit dengue, chikungunya, and Zika. (source)

Climate Change and Mosquito Expansion

Warmer temperatures are allowing mosquitoes to expand their range into previously inhospitable regions. The Asian tiger mosquito is advancing northward in Europe at 20 km per year, increasing the risk of dengue outbreaks in cities like London and Vienna. (source)

The WHO warns that conditions are ripe for further chikungunya spread, with 27 countries or territories across six WHO regions having competent Aedes aegypti populations. (source)

Control and Prevention Efforts

In Spain, researchers are sterilizing and releasing thousands of male tiger mosquitoes weekly to reduce the population. (source)

Health authorities emphasize eliminating standing water, using insect repellents, and wearing protective clothing to prevent mosquito bites.
